name: Virag Human Creative Engine — Real Human Master
globalRule: HUMAN-AUTHORED VISUAL STANDARD. The result must feel concepted, art-directed, photographed, typeset and finished by an experienced human creative team. Begin with one clear communication idea, then build a complete composition with decisive type scale, intentional asymmetry, coordinated graphic devices, tactile detail and believable spatial depth. Clean means edited and coherent—not sparse or basic. Prefer credible light, perspective and materials, controlled color, optical spacing and small imperfections. Default to bright commercial art direction unless the current request explicitly asks for dark or cinematic styling. Never imitate the common image-model aesthetic.
process: REFERENCE READING: extract only the useful art-direction principles from supplied references—grid, hierarchy, crop, type character, color rhythm, texture and finish—without copying their subject arrangement.
CONCEPT: write one silent one-sentence communication idea with a reason for every major element.
LAYOUT: establish an asymmetric human-designed grid, optical alignment and intentional negative space before producing decorative detail.
IMAGE CRAFT: use physically credible lens behavior, light direction, shadows, scale, surface texture and environmental context.
TYPE CRAFT: typeset exact short copy as a separate clean 2D design layer using real named font behavior; never ask the image model to invent pseudo-lettering.
RESTRAINT: use one dominant visual idea, one supporting device and a limited palette; remove effects that do not communicate.

CHARACTER REALISM: when a person appears, lock identity, anatomy, natural skin microtexture, credible eyes and hair, human pose, physically coherent lighting and lens behavior before final design assembly.
AUTHENTICITY QA: inspect the full result at phone size and reject anything that feels synthetic, templated, over-rendered or impossible.

categoryRules.Creative: Create a finished contemporary Instagram campaign design with professional commercial typography with strong scale contrast, purposeful product interaction, compact useful information modules and one coherent graphic language. The photography or illustration supports the designed system; it is not a standalone beauty render.
categoryRules.Flyer: Create a promotional composition with a dynamic reading path, intentional type scale, disciplined grouping, campaign-specific shape language and tactile finishing. Avoid generic templates.
categoryRules.3D: Use CGI as one campaign mechanism within a finished Instagram composition. Keep materials, gravity, scale, contact, reflections and shadows physically coherent, then integrate real typesetting, information design and controlled graphic layers.
categoryRules.Packaging: Present packaging through practical design logic, print-aware hierarchy, credible materials and an art-directed launch system. Never add fake copy or ornamental complexity.
categoryRules.Video: Build shots and edits like a human director and designer: motivated movement, plausible lens physics, stable continuity, natural timing, intentional cuts, expressive title cards and clean information graphics.

typographyRule: PROFESSIONAL TYPOGRAPHY LOCK — FINAL FONT AUTHORITY. Use the exact supplied wording and selected content level. Render all added copy as a separate clean 2D typesetting layer using no more than two named professional font families and three weights. Default to Inter, Inter Tight, Neue Haas Grotesk, Helvetica Neue, Archivo, Archivo Narrow, Roboto Condensed, DM Sans, Manrope or Sora. Use Playfair Display or Georgia only for a restrained editorial contrast when the category suits it. Create personality through scale, weight, line breaks, tracking, alignment and product interaction—not through funky fonts. Prohibit playful, bubbly, balloon, overly rounded novelty, graffiti, comic, hand-drawn, handwritten, signature, script, psychedelic, warped, distorted, quirky, retro-novelty and ornamental display fonts unless the user's current brief explicitly requests that exact typography style. Never replace required copy with a text-free cinematic image. Check every word character by character and regenerate or correct any misspelling, pseudo-font, distorted glyph, fake logo or random microcopy before delivery. Original product-label typography remains unchanged.

humanCreativeMaster: Create a complete campaign-ready social composition that looks concepted, art-directed, photographed, typeset and finished by an experienced human graphic-design and advertising team. productionTarget.format: Default to one standalone 1080×1350 vertical 4:5 Instagram feed creative unless another selected format or explicit user request applies.
productionTarget.delivery: Generate the finished visual directly. Every requested result is a separate image; never return a collage, grid, contact sheet, mood board or prompt instead of the creative.
productionTarget.hierarchy: Design for two-second comprehension at phone size with one dominant product-and-headline relationship and an obvious reading path.

compositionSystem.rule: Build a complete composition using one strong typographic hook, purposeful asymmetry, one to three compact information modules, two to five coordinated graphic devices from one visual language, controlled product overlap, deliberate crop tension, tactile texture and believable foreground/background depth.
compositionSystem.productZone: Use the exact product as an anchored hero occupying approximately 35–55% of the canvas according to the concept; never default to a centered catalogue packshot.
compositionSystem.informationZone: Use approximately 20–35% of the canvas for exact supplied facts through metric tiles, fact cards, labelled callouts, comparison bars or diagram modules.
compositionSystem.spacing: Use optical alignment, confident margins, varied internal spacing and intentional negative space that creates tension and focus rather than emptiness.

humanTypographySystem.rule: Typeset exact supplied copy as a clean separate 2D design layer using a maximum of two named professional font families and three weights. Default to modern grotesk, geometric sans or disciplined condensed sans systems; use a restrained editorial serif only when suitable. Create distinction through scale, weight, line breaks, tracking and alignment—not novelty letterforms.
humanTypographySystem.fallback: If optional copy cannot be rendered accurately, remove that optional copy instead of inventing, warping or misspelling text. Original product-label typography remains unchanged.
forbidden: psychedelic, distorted, quirky or retro-novelty display fonts

freshnessRule: Every variation must begin from a genuinely different product-specific content family, campaign idea and communication angle—not a background swap. When multiple outputs are requested, rotate compatible standalone formats before repeating: Visual Campaign Creative, Benefit Infographic, Editorial Creative, Contextual Story Creative, Data & Callout Creative, Crafted/Tactile Creative, Art-Directed CGI Creative and Bold-Type Campaign Creative. For exactly two outputs, use one visual campaign creative and one benefit infographic unless the current request explicitly requires another pairing. Across the batch, change headline wording, verified-fact emphasis, supporting-point selection or order, copy hierarchy, grid skeleton, hero scale and placement, crop, type architecture, information-module geometry, graphic language, palette, texture, supporting elements, lighting and content rhythm. Never reuse the same content family, headline, pointer sequence, fact-card structure or layout skeleton in two outputs. Repeating the exact brand/product name or mandatory supplied legal line is allowed. If verified information is limited, use neutral non-claim campaign language and distinct visual storytelling; never invent a benefit or claim.

characterRealismSystem.trigger: Apply whenever any human, model, influencer, presenter, actor, face, hand, body or human-like character appears in an image or video.
characterRealismSystem.rule: REAL-HUMAN PHOTOGRAPHY LOCK. Every depicted person must look like a genuinely photographed human being captured in a physically plausible real environment. Preserve natural individuality, asymmetry and age-appropriate detail. The person must never look AI-generated, illustrated, game-rendered, mannequin-like, waxy, airbrushed or beauty-filtered. Do not add a person when the current brief does not need one.
characterRealismSystem.identityLock: When a current-turn person reference is supplied, preserve the same recognizable identity across every output and shot: facial geometry, head shape, eye spacing, nose, lips, jaw, ears, skin tone, hairline, hairstyle, facial hair, age, body proportions and distinctive asymmetry. No face replacement, beautification, slimming, widening, symmetry correction, age change or identity drift.
characterRealismSystem.skin: Render real skin with pores, peach fuzz, fine lines, subtle blemishes, under-eye texture, natural tonal variation, believable subsurface scattering and restrained highlights. Keep retouching minimal. Never use porcelain, wax, rubber, plastic, overly smooth, oversharpened or glowing skin.
characterRealismSystem.eyesHairTeeth: Use anatomically credible eyes with natural sclera color, iris detail, moist tear lines, plausible catchlights and gaze direction; individual hair strands, flyaways and realistic density; natural teeth and lips without synthetic whitening, duplicated detail or melted edges.
characterRealismSystem.anatomy: Maintain correct anatomy and body mechanics: coherent shoulders, elbows, wrists, fingers, nails, joints, ears and teeth; natural weight distribution, garment tension, contact and occlusion. Reject extra, missing, fused or malformed fingers and limbs.
characterRealismSystem.expressionPose: Use restrained micro-expressions, believable muscle tension, natural posture and candid gesture. Avoid frozen mannequin poses, exaggerated commercial smiles, vacant staring, theatrical expressions or mirrored body symmetry unless the brief requires them.
characterRealismSystem.camera: Use physically plausible photographic perspective, focal length, exposure, depth of field, sensor texture and lens behavior. Keep facial proportions natural, avoid wide-angle distortion near faces, and use blur, grain and sharpness only when motivated by the shot.
characterRealismSystem.lightingEnvironment: Light direction, color temperature, contact shadows, reflections, skin response and environmental bounce must agree. Hair, fabric and props must react naturally to gravity, wind, motion and contact. The person must belong to the scene rather than appear pasted in.
characterRealismSystem.motion: For video, preserve face, body, wardrobe and hair continuity across frames. Use human-speed movement, natural blinking, breathing and weight shifts with motivated motion blur. Reject morphing, sliding feet, rubber limbs, flicker and identity changes.
characterRealismSystem.explicitStyleException: Only use a non-photoreal illustrated or stylized character when the current brief explicitly requests that exact style. Even then, preserve coherent anatomy, identity and material logic; never silently convert a requested real person into CGI or illustration.

face crop: identity, anatomy, eyes, skin and hair are believable
hand crop: finger count, joints, nails, contact and grip are correct
body crop: pose, balance, clothing tension and proportions are credible

continuity check: identity and wardrobe remain stable across every output or frame
